species.blurb: A secretive marsh bird that calls from pickleweed and cordgrass. Once called California Clapper Rail; still one of the refuge's signature endangered shorebirds.
A tiny endemic rodent that lives only in Bay Area tidal marshes. Don Edwards protects critical pickleweed habitat for this federally endangered species.
A small shorebird that nests on salt-pond levees and open flats. Look for them quietly running along pale shorelines — please keep distance from nesting areas.
